name: fs-uae
why: An Amiga emulator opens a window into old-school machines and their software, though emulators are a familiar niche.

brief.what_it_is: FS-UAE is a cross-platform Amiga emulator for Windows, macOS and Linux (including Raspberry Pi), with a particular focus on games. It ships with a user-friendly, database-driven launcher and an optional arcade-mode frontend. The homepage lists version 3.2.35 as the latest stable release, and an early alpha of FS-UAE 5 is also available. The Homebrew package installs two executables, fs-uae and fs-uae-device-helper.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a games-focused Amiga emulator that is easy to use through a launcher and an arcade frontend. The README for FS-UAE 5 says the goal is for it to eventually do everything FS-UAE 3 did, and more.
brief.how_it_works: FS-UAE 5 is built with SDL3 and includes a GUI system written in Python. The Python UI runs in a separate thread and renders into offscreen images that are composited with the emulator's video output in the same window, so the UI can stay active while emulation runs. Emulation core code is derived from WinUAE.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is the easy route (brew install fs-uae). Building from source needs gettext, glib, libmpeg, libpng, libsamplerate, portmidi, Python, SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_ttf, plus autoconf/automake for bootstrap. The homepage links to Amiga Forever for purchasing legal Kickstart ROMs, which suggests you will need Kickstart ROM files to run Amiga software; the README does not spell this out. No first-run steps were seen.
brief.standout: The launcher is database-driven, and FS-UAE 5 adds an arcade frontend and a Python-based GUI system. The README says floppy images can now be inserted during emulation via native file dialogs, and that floppy images are writable by default.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage lists FS-UAE 3.2.35 released 2025-09-07, Launcher 3.2.20 released 2025-09-06, and FS-UAE 5 alpha releases 2025-09-05. The news list also shows a gap back to 2021-12-19, so the stable branch was quiet for years before this burst. I did not see a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: FS-UAE 5 is an early alpha. Its README lists almost no configurability, no v-sync, no shader or zoom or aspect-ratio options, no .fs-uae config loading, no custom input mapping, no net play, and no gamepad UI yet. The GitHub landing page shows a WinUAE-derived Windows build guide (Visual Studio 2017, WDK, NASM) that is not relevant to macOS or Linux users. The README says the source build is not yet officially documented for installation.
quotes: The cross-platform Amiga emulator for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a particular focus on games.
Floppy images will now be writable by default (perhaps the second-most requested feature).
Almost no configurability (yet) - no settings to speak of. What you see is what you get (this will change, of course).
